html:
The map's label, in its 1938 snapshot, for Ethiopia under Italian occupation, from 1936 to 1941, part of Italian East Africa.

Mussolini invaded in October 1935 to avenge the defeat at Adwa and win an empire. In the Second Italo-Ethiopian War the Italians used aircraft and poison gas, and took Addis Ababa in May 1936. Emperor Haile Selassie went into exile and appealed to the League of Nations, whose weak sanctions failed.

Occupation was brutal. After an attempt on the life of the viceroy Graziani in February 1937, Italian troops and settlers killed thousands of people in Addis Ababa. Ethiopian resistance fighters, the Arbegnoch, held much of the countryside. In 1941, during World War II, British, Commonwealth and Ethiopian forces drove the Italians out, and Haile Selassie returned to his capital that May. The Ethiopian Empire was restored.
